To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
coagulase negative staphylococcus are common contaminants of milk and can produce enterotoxins.
coagulase negative staphylococcus (CNS) can produce staphylococcocal enterotoxin (SE) and biofilm, and that CNS can be a source of SE and biofilm in milk and milk-derived products.
coagulase negative staphylococi isolated from bovine milk are able to produce staphylococal enterotoxins as well as biofilms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the pathogenic potential of CNS, and it could represent a first step for a more detailed analysis of the pathogenicity of CNS in milk and milk derivatives, and for their possible use as starter cultures in the food industry.
the identification and molecular characterization of CNS, isolated from bovine bulk milk, with the aim of evaluating the potential role of CNS as enterotoxigenics and biofilm producers.
the identification of genes encoding for the production of enterotoxigenicity, TSST- 1, and biofilms production in CNS from bovine bulk milk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
enterotoxins production by CNS in milk is not an uncommon event.
the CNS isolated from bulk tank milk are able to produce enterotoxins as well as biofilms.
the presence of enterotoxin genes is not a rare event among CNS isolated from bovine milk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CNS are present in bovine bulk tank milks and that they can produce enterotoxins.
the presence of enterotoxigenicity genes and biofilm production among CNS from bovine bulk milk could represent a potential source for contamination of milk and milk products.
coagulase negative staphylococcus are opportunistic pathogens and they are present in the bovine bulk tank milks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNS are able to produce staphylococcus enterotoxins in milk.
CNS are able to produce superantigens and biofilm, and that these virulence factors can be detected in CNS from bovine milk.
CNS could represent a reservoir of pathogenic factors, which could be transferred to S. aureus, enhancing its pathogenicity.
